subject: Mutual Action Plan: security gates, DPA carveouts and acceptance escape-hatches
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@fincore.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: security+procurement@fincore.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + security acceptance windows

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our initial MAP draft (MAP_Draft_FinCore_v1.pdf) — it contains the milestones we need to clear from a security and procurement perspective so we can close and move into production. High level asks relevant to Redwood: 

- SOC 2: we'd like the report and a short controls summary by the time of contract signature (our procurement target is 3 business days after signed SOW). If you have a hosted SOC2 summary let us know.
- SIG/CAIQ: completion of the questionnaire and gap responses during the evaluation (target 10 business days).
- DPA: our legal team will share a redline; can you confirm turnaround window for a counter-redline?
- Data retention: we need explicit retention windows for session logs, KV cache snapshots, and model input artifacts. We also need to discuss an "escape-hatch" for retention carveouts if we surface a high-volume debugging window.

Can you propose a MAP timeline that locks down these acceptance gates and an explicit fallback plan if SOC 2 delivery slips? We are sensitive to launch timing, so a staged production (sandbox -> limited prod -> full prod) is acceptable but needs clear acceptance criteria and SLA credit mechanics.

Appreciate it — copied security+procurement to keep runs transparent.

Best,
Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Technical Procurement
FinCore Financial

Attachment: MAP_Draft_FinCore_v1.pdf (stub)

From: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@fincore.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + security acceptance windows

Emma — thanks for the MAP and the clear ask list. I pulled together an initial runbook and milestone timeline (see attached proposed_map_connor.xlsx). High-level answers below so procurement and legal can align: 

- SOC 2: we can provide the SOC 2 Type II report summary and cover letter within 3 business days of your request; a full report requires our compliance team sign-off but summary + controls matrix can be shared immediately (Attachment: SOC2_2026_summary.pdf).
- SIG/CAIQ: we commit to completing the CAIQ sections that map to your risk profile within 10 business days. If you need an accelerated path we can prioritize the top 10 control families and deliver within 5 business days for the initial pass.
- DPA redline turnaround: Redwood legal can review and provide a counter-redline within 2 business days of receiving your edit. For substantive carveouts we escalate to Legal + Product and will flag any non-standard clauses.
- Data retention defaults: session logs (30 days), KV/cache snapshots (90 days), model input artifacts (30 days) with optional 365-day archival for transaction metadata on request. For debugging windows we can agree to a temporary short-term extension (escape-hatch) limited to a named incident and with additional safeguards (PII scrubbing + HMAC-based access control).

Proposed MAP milestones (draft):
- T0 (today): MAP agreed in principle.
- T0+3bd: SOC 2 summary delivered.
- T0+10bd: SIG/CAIQ initial responses.
- T0+14bd: DPA counter-redline.
- T0+21bd: Security acceptance sign-off or mutual go/no-go; if SOC2 delayed, proceed to staged rollout option below.

Staged rollout / fallback option (if SOC2 or SIG delayed):
1) Sandbox integration (no real PII) — immediate.
2) Limited production (subset of traffic, model routing to hosted variant, additional logging retention controls) — allowed with signed exception and SLA crediting if acceptance gates miss targets.
3) Full production once SOC2 + SIG gates are closed.

I've attached a proposed MAP spreadsheet that enumerates owners and acceptance criteria. Laura, Rishi — can you review the DPA/redline path and the escape-hatch language (temporary retention extensions with PII scrubbing)?

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_map_connor.xlsx (stub); SOC2_2026_summary.pdf (stub)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@fincore.com>
Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + security acceptance windows

Emma — looping in a short DPA note. We received the redline and have prepared a counter-redline (redline_dpa_connor_v2.docx attached). Key legal items: 

- EU residency carveout: Redwood supports customer-requested data residency via our Private deployment offering. For hosted customers, we propose contractual commitments around logical separation, encryption, and cross-border transfer safeguards; full residency is available as an add-on.
- Retention escape-hatch: we are willing to include a limited, time-boxed retention exception (for debugging incidents only) subject to: 1) written escalation owner; 2) PII minimization (automatic redaction pipeline); 3) access auditing (KMS/HSM-backed keys); and 4) post-incident purge schedule.
- SLA credits: if any of the security deliverables (SOC2 summary, SIG responses, DPA counter) slip beyond the MAP windows and you elect to proceed with staged production, we will include a carveout for SLA credits tied to acceptance delay. The credit mechanics are standard (service credits scaled by impacted tokens/requests) and are in the DPA redline.

If those three points look ok we can mark the DPA as ready for signature after minor edits. Rishi — suggest we finalize the explicit audit evidence links (control owners + evidence paths) and include them in the MAP appendix.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_dpa_connor_v2.docx (stub)

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@fincore.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, security+procurement@fincore.com
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + security acceptance windows

Connor/Laura — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear fallback language. Two quick confirmations before we lock: 

1) The escape-hatch operational detail: for the temporary retention extension during a named debugging incident, can you confirm who is the operational owner on Redwood's side (name + email) and the maximum extension period? FINCORE policy requires a named owner and a 14-day max extension unless otherwise approved by our CISO.

2) SLA credits: can you include a short example calculation in the MAP appendix (e.g., missed acceptance results in X% credit applied pro-rata for Y days)? That will help our procurement sign-off.

If those two items are satisfied we will sign the MAP and move the SOW into signature. We prefer the staged rollout approach you provided.

Best,
Emma

On Thu, 19 Aug 2027 at 12:42 PM connor.obrien@redwood.ai wrote:
> Emma — quick answers inline:
>
> 1) Operational owner for escape-hatch: Rishi Malhotra (rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai) — will be the escalation contact and will coordinate access audits and the purge schedule. Maximum extension period we agree to is 14 days by default; any longer requires CISO-level approval.
>
> 2) SLA credit example: we've added a worked example to the MAP appendix (see proposed_map_connor.xlsx) but quick summary: a missed acceptance gate triggers a tiered credit (2% of monthly committed fee for each business day beyond agreed acceptance up to a 20% cap). Credits prorate based on affected routes/throughput.
>
> We're happy to finalize — I'll update the MAP spreadsheet with the named owner and the SLA worked example and circulate a sign-ready packet.
>
> Connor
